summary: This bill directs the Departments of the Interior and Agriculture to standardize data formats, digitize detailed maps of federal waterway access points, restrictions on boats and activities, and fishing rules, and publish them online for public use within five years, with regular updates and annual progress reports to Congress.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates federal agencies (Secretaries of Agriculture and Interior) to develop interagency data standards, digitize and publish extensive GIS data on Federal waterway restrictions, access, and fishing info online within specified timelines (30 months for standards, 5 years for data), update it regularly (twice yearly or real-time), allow public comments, cooperate with partners including private sector/third parties/USGS, and submit annual reports to Congress through 2034. This imposes new administrative burdens and resource requirements on agencies, likely increasing government spending for personnel, technology, contracts, and data management, despite phrases like 'to the maximum extent practicable' and leveraging existing efforts/data. No funding cuts, offsets, or reductions mentioned; it's purely additive mandates. Thus, minor expansion of government spending.

The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue in any form. It focuses solely on data standardization and publication for recreational access to federal waterways.
No mention of healthcare, insurance, medical coverage, providers, or related policies. The bill is exclusively about recreational data on federal waterways.
No references to guns, firearms, Second Amendment, regulations, or rights. Entirely unrelated to public safety or weapons.
No content on immigration, borders, visas, enforcement, or protections. Focus is on domestic federal waterway recreation data.
No provisions or language touching on abortion, reproductive rights, or related healthcare issues.
No involvement with military, defense budget, armed forces, or national security spending. Agencies involved manage civilian lands/waters.

The bill deals with data on existing federal waterway restrictions (e.g., no-wake zones, closures, motorized limits) and fishing restrictions, which often stem from environmental protections, but it only requires standardization, digitization, and public publication of current rules without altering, expanding, or limiting any regulations, authorities, or access (explicitly stated in Section 7). It promotes transparency for recreation but has no direct policy impact on environmental protections or climate measures.
No relation to welfare, food stamps, unemployment, or social programs. Purely administrative for outdoor recreation data.
No educational funding, schools, curricula, or federal involvement in education mentioned.
No drug-related content, enforcement, decriminalization, or substances.
No criminal penalties, policing, sentencing, or justice reform elements.
No trade, tariffs, imports/exports, or globalization issues.
While it implies some added spending (see government_spending), it does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy directly; no prioritization of debt or acceptance of deficits.
No protections, discriminations, or rights related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
Domestic focus only; no foreign assistance or international aid.
No voting access, elections, or integrity measures.

Involves digitizing/publishing GIS data online via tech/third parties, public comments process, and excludes sensitive archaeological data disclosure. Promotes public access to govt data (less privacy for public lands info) with minimal regs on tech partners, but primarily govt transparency mandate, not tech industry regulation or broad privacy policy.
No worker protections, unions, or labor flexibility issues; third-party agreements possible but not labor-focused.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or discrimination provisions.
